body.statement:
For every valid finite binary-rational encoding \(\mathfrak E\) and every \(0<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}<1\), the deterministic nested interval Bellman algorithm in the corrected certificate handle terminates and returns rational endpoints, an attained finite-net prior \(\lambda\), and a finite mixture of net Bayes controls \(u\).  Its cumulative lower and upper sequences are respectively nondecreasing and nonincreasing, converge to \(V\), and at termination satisfy
\[
 \underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad
 \overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}.
\]
The certificate ledger records the actual terminal-regularization, guard-exit, time-discretization, interpolation and control-mesh, Gaussian-cell, Gaussian-tail, oracle and linear-program, recovered-policy, prior-net, and outward-rounding bounds.  The returned mixture is re-evaluated by an independent fixed-policy interval recursion, which certifies \(\max_{1\leq m\leq M}r_m(u)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\).  For this returned mixture, boundary-stable transfer gives predictable finite-horizon policies \(\pi_n\) satisfying
\[
 \max_{1\leq m\leq M}r_{n,m}(\pi_n)
 \leq \overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1)
 \qquad(n\to\infty).
\]
No closed-form mesh size, arithmetic complexity bound, or convergence rate is asserted.
body.justification: The theorem gives a reproducible epsilon certificate because every scaled-datum continuity contribution is computed from the corrected modulus, every accepted endpoint is backed by a candidate-specific rational ledger, and the returned policy mixture is independently re-evaluated.
body.gap: Baas--ter Schure--van Rosmalen's scalar e-value dynamic program and Rosenblum--Fang--Liu's discretized two-stage sparse program are complementary donors. Arithmetic e-value averaging and scalar time-uniform boundaries are also borrowed components. None supplies this controlled-diffusion missed-discovery-regret certificate, its candidate-specific validated lower and upper ledger, or the independent recovered-policy evaluation.
body.consumer: The certified interval, least-favorable net prior, and independently checked policy mixture can accompany rpact recruitment tables and interAdapt finite-stage decision rules.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(\ell_{m,\delta}^-\) and \(\ell_{m,\delta}^+\) for the losses in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}terminal\text{-}envelopes}\).  For every \(a\in\mathbb R\),
\[
 f_\delta^-(a)\leq\mathbf1\{a<0\}\leq f_\delta^+(a).             \tag{35}
\]
Multiplication by the nonnegative weights \(w_j\mathbf1\{h_j^m>0\}\), followed by summation, gives
\[
 0\leq\ell_{m,\delta}^-\leq\ell_m\leq
 \ell_{m,\delta}^+\leq1.                                        \tag{36}
\]
If \(c_{m,\delta}^\pm\) denotes the corresponding oracle value, taking infima in (36) yields
\[
 B_\delta^-(\lambda)\leq B(\lambda)\leq B_\delta^+(\lambda),
 \qquad
 c_{m,\delta}^-\leq c_m\leq c_{m,\delta}^+.                     \tag{37}
\]
These are bounds on observed-law design functionals and do not redefine the causal regret target \(V\).

\emph{The two continuity moduli.}
Put \(c_H=H+H^2/2\), \(s_k=x_k-q_k/2\), and \(e_I=\lvert I\rvert^{-1}\sum_{k\in I}\exp(s_k)\).  Along a line segment in \((x,q)\), either envelope composed with \(a_j=\min_{I\ni j}e_I-20\) is absolutely continuous.  Wherever its derivative is nonzero, an active intersection obeys
\[
 19<20-\delta\leq e_I\leq20+\delta<21.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \sum_{k\in I}\left\lvert\frac{\partial e_I}{\partial x_k}\right\rvert<21,
 \qquad
 \sum_{k\in I}\left\lvert\frac{\partial e_I}{\partial q_k}\right\rvert<\frac{21}{2}.
\]
Since the envelope slope is at most \(1/\delta\), integration along the segment gives the conservative bound
\[
 \lvert\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm(x,q)-\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm(x',q')\rvert
 \leq\frac{32}{\delta}\lVert(x,q)-(x',q')\rVert_\infty.          \tag{38}
\]
No division by an allocation clock is used.

For the likelihoods in the frozen core,
\[
 d\log Z_m=\sum_jh_j^m\,dx_j-\frac12\sum_j(h_j^m)^2\,dq_j,
\]
and hence, when the state displacement has sup norm at most \(d\),
\[
 \lvert\log Z_m-\log Z_m'\rvert\leq Kc_Hd.                       \tag{39}
\]
Differentiating the posterior weights gives
\[
 db_m^\lambda=b_m^\lambda\left(d\log Z_m-
 \sum_rb_r^\lambda d\log Z_r\right),
\]
so
\[
 \sum_m\lvert db_m^\lambda\rvert\leq2Kc_Hd.                     \tag{40}
\]
This remains valid when prior coordinates vanish.  Thus the normalized posterior terminal payoff \(g=\sum_mb_m^\lambda\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm\) has modulus
\[
 \Omega_\delta(d)=
 \min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+2Kc_H\right)d\right\}.   \tag{41}
\]

Now fix a guard box and let
\[
 C_G=\max_{\text{guard box}}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m,\qquad
 S=\frac{\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m}{C_G}.
\]
Along every segment contained in the guard box, \(0\leq S\leq1\).  Moreover, the logarithmic derivative of \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\) is the posterior-weighted average of the logarithmic derivatives of the \(Z_m\)'s.  Equation (39) therefore gives
\[
 \lvert S-S'\rvert\leq Kc_Hd.                                   \tag{42}
\]
Since \(0\leq g,g',S,S'\leq1\),
\[
 \lvert Sg-S'g'\rvert\leq \lvert g-g'\rvert+\lvert S-S'\rvert.
\]
Combining this inequality with (41)--(42) proves that the scaled unnormalized reference datum \(Sg\) has the corrected modulus
\[
 \widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)=
 \min\!\left\{1,\left(\frac{32}{\delta}+3Kc_H\right)d\right\}.   \tag{43}
\]
The outer minimum is essential: once the linear expression reaches one, the range bound \(0\leq Sg\leq1\) is used.

The relevant modulus propagates backward.  Couple two processes started from states at the same time by using the same future noise and feeding the second policy the first history translated by the initial state difference.  Their controls coincide and their terminal score--clock difference equals the initial difference.  Equations (38)--(43), followed by taking infima in both directions, give \(\Omega_\delta\) for the normalized posterior value and \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\) for every scaled unnormalized continuation value.  The scaled reference-law computation below therefore uses \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\) in every interpolation, control-continuity, mollification, Bellman-residual, finite-horizon accumulation, fixed-policy, and point-mass-oracle bound.  The coupling remains valid on zero-allocation faces.

\emph{Validated finite recursion.}
Under the zero-drift reference law, bounded predictability makes
\[
 Z_m(X(t),Q(t))=
 \exp\!\left\{\sum_jh_j^mX_j(t)
 -\frac12\sum_j(h_j^m)^2Q_j(t)\right\}                           \tag{44}
\]
a mean-one likelihood process.  Successive Gaussian conditioning proves this for simple predictable controls.  Approximation in stochastic-integral norm proves it for general controls because the integrands have energy bounded by \(H^2\).  Thus, for bounded terminal \(R\),
\[
 \mathbb E_m^u[R]=\mathbb E_0^u[Z_m(X(1),Q(1))R].                \tag{45}
\]
The reference terminal datum is consequently \(\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm=C_GSg\).  After division by \(C_G\), its range is \([0,1]\).  At first guard exit the scaled conditional continuation therefore lies in \([0,1]\); the algorithm uses this exterior interval and makes no clamping assertion.

Suppose the vertices \(v\) of a viable state cell carry intervals enclosing a scaled continuation function \(F\), and \(y\) has multilinear barycentric weights \(\beta_v\).  If the cell diameter is \(d\), (43) gives
\[
 \left\lvert F(y)-\sum_v\beta_vF(v)\right\rvert
 \leq\sum_v\beta_v\widetilde\Omega_\delta(\lVert y-v\rVert_\infty)
 \leq\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d).                                \tag{46}
\]
Thus the barycentric interval enlarged by the corrected modulus encloses \(F(y)\).

For a time increment \(a>0\), constant allocation \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\), and standard Gaussian \(z\), the reference transition is
\[
 (x,q)\longmapsto
 \bigl(x+(av)^{1/2}\mathbin\odot z,\ q+av\bigr).                 \tag{47}
\]
For each retained Gaussian cell, interval arithmetic encloses the entire image of (47).  Multiplying its nonnegative continuation interval by an outward-rounded probability interval and summing outward preserves enclosure; omitted mass is multiplied by \([0,1]\).  Coupling allocations \(v,v'\) with the same \(z\), using \((\sqrt p-\sqrt q)^2\leq\lvert p-q\rvert\), bounds the scaled control-net error by
\[
 \mathbb E\,\widetilde\Omega_\delta\!\left(
 a\lVert v-v'\rVert_1+\sqrt{a\lVert v-v'\rVert_1}\,\lVert z\rVert_2\right).
                                                                    \tag{48}
\]
Bounded convergence makes (48) tend uniformly to zero with the control-net radius.  Taking the minimum of lower endpoints minus this error and of upper endpoints plus this error encloses the Bellman infimum over the whole simplex.  Backward induction using (46)--(48) proves enclosure at every time level.  The identical argument, with the same corrected modulus, validates fixed-policy and point-mass-oracle recursions.  Gaussian cell probabilities have effective rational outward bounds obtained from rational Taylor bounds for \(\exp(-z^2/2)\) on bounded cells; omitted Gaussian mass is assigned adversarially in \([0,1]\).

\emph{Passage to continuous time.}
Let \(P_a^v\) denote the Gaussian operator in (47), and put
\[
 \mathcal L^v\phi=\frac12\sum_jv_j\partial_{x_jx_j}\phi+
 \sum_jv_j\partial_{q_j}\phi.                                   \tag{49}
\]
For the exact regularized recursion on a partition \(0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=1\), with \(a_l=t_{l+1}-t_l\),
\[
 J_l=\min_{v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)}P_{a_l}^vJ_{l+1},
 \qquad
 J_l\leq P_{a_l}^vJ_{l+1}\quad\text{for every }v.               \tag{50}
\]
Convolve the scaled multilinear lower interpolants on the inner score box with a rational compactly supported \(C^3\) tensor mollifier of radius \(\kappa\), whose support lies in the guard box.  Its terminal and intermediate mollification errors are bounded by \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(\kappa)\), not by (41).  Convolution commutes with \(P_a^v\).  If the one-layer interval error, recomputed using (43), is \(\xi_l\), subtracting \(\sum_{s\geq l}\xi_s\) restores the second inequality in (50) for the smoothed lower interpolants.  Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives
\[
 P_a^v\phi-\phi-a\mathcal L^v\phi=\mathcal R_a^v(\phi).          \tag{51}
\]
Derivative intervals of the mollified interpolant and truncated Gaussian moments give outward rational bounds for \(\mathcal R_a^v\).  For fixed \(\kappa\), the score remainder is bounded by a computable multiple of \(a^{3/2}\kappa^{-3}\), the clock remainder by a computable multiple of \(a^2\kappa^{-2}\), and the interpolation contribution by the corrected \(\xi_l\).  The checked rational refinements include
\[
 \max_la_l\downarrow0,\quad
 \sum_l\xi_l\downarrow0,\quad
 \max_l\frac{\xi_l}{a_l}\downarrow0,\quad
 \kappa\downarrow0,\quad
 \max_la_l^{1/2}\kappa^{-3}\downarrow0.                          \tag{52}
\]
Because \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta(d)\to0\) as \(d\downarrow0\) for fixed \(\delta\), such refinements exist.

Linear interpolation in time then gives computable errors \(e_T\geq0\) and \(e_B(t)\geq0\) such that
\[
 \phi^-(1,\cdot)\leq
 C_G^{-1}\sum_m\lambda_mZ_m\ell_{m,\delta}^\pm,\quad
 \phi^-\leq0\ \text{on the guard boundary},\quad
 \partial_t\phi^-+\mathcal L^v\phi^-\geq-e_B(t)                 \tag{53}
\]
for every \(v\in\Delta(\mathcal J)\), and
\[
 e_T+\int_0^1e_B(t)\,dt\longrightarrow0.                        \tag{54}
\]
For simple predictable controls stopped at guard exit, successive conditional Gaussian integrations and (51) telescope.  Since \(\mathcal L^u=\sum_ju_j\mathcal L^{e_j}\), every such control has scaled risk at least
\[
 \phi^-(0,0,0)-\int_0^1e_B(t)\,dt.                              \tag{55}
\]
All quantities are bounded on the guard box, so stochastic-integral approximation extends (55) to every progressively measurable control.  This validates the lower endpoint directly and does not invoke global generalized-terminal comparison.

For the upper endpoint, the grid recursion selects a predictable piecewise-constant policy, and the independent fixed-policy recursion, again using (43), encloses its actual risk.  Predictable simple simplex processes \(v^{(N)}\) approximate every admissible control \(u\) with
\[
 \mathbb E\int_0^1\lVert u(t)-v^{(N)}(t)\rVert_1\,dt\longrightarrow0. \tag{56}
\]
The Itô isometry and the square-root inequality give
\[
 \mathbb E\lVert Q^u(1)-Q^{v^{(N)}}(1)\rVert_1\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \sum_j\mathbb E\left\lvert
 \int_0^1(\sqrt{u_j(t)}-\sqrt{v_j^{(N)}(t)})\,dW_j(t)
 \right\rvert^2\longrightarrow0.                               \tag{57}
\]
The scenario drift difference is at most \(H\) times the first quantity.  Equations (38) and (57) yield convergence of every regularized scenario risk, uniformly over the finite scenario list.  Approximating the finitely many simple action values by the rational control net using (48) completes the upper approximation.  Combining it with (54)--(55) proves convergence of the two regularized Bellman endpoints to the same continuous-control value.  At a fixed partition, backward conditioning makes the current score, clock, and likelihood vector a sufficient Markov state.  If \(v_j=0\), (47) fixes coordinate \(j\) and (49) gives it zero coefficient; no forced exploration is required.

\emph{Guard control.}
Under scenario \(m\),
\[
 X_j(t)=h_j^mQ_j(t)+M_j(t),\qquad
 M_j(t)=\int_0^t\sqrt{u_j(s)}\,dW_j(s),\qquad0\leq Q_j(t)\leq1.
\]
Successive Gaussian conditioning and simple-process approximation show that \(\exp\{\theta M_j(t)-\theta^2Q_j(t)/2\}\) is a mean-one nonnegative martingale.  Applying Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}howard\text{-}linear\text{-}boundary}\) to both signs and using \(\lvert h_j^m\rvert\leq H\) gives, uniformly over \(m\) and \(u\),
\[
 \Pr_m^u\!\left\{\max_j\sup_{t\leq1}\lvert X_j(t)\rvert>G\right\}
 \leq2K\exp\!\left\{-\frac{(G-H)^2}{2}\right\},\qquad G>H.       \tag{58}
\]
Thus exterior intervals affect risk only through the certified probability in (58), which vanishes as \(G\to\infty\).

\emph{Minimax assembly and termination.}
Define
\[
 \mathcal G(\lambda)=B(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_m
 =\inf_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_m\lambda_mr_m(u).                   \tag{59}
\]
Because \(r_m(u)\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \lvert\mathcal G(\lambda)-\mathcal G(\lambda')\rvert
 \leq\lVert\lambda-\lambda'\rVert_1.                            \tag{60}
\]
The rational simplex net with denominator \(D\) contains every point mass and has \(\ell_1\)-radius at most \(2(M-1)/D\).  The already established Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}least\text{-}favorable\text{-}saddle}\) gives
\[
 V=\max_{\lambda\in\Delta_M}\mathcal G(\lambda).                \tag{61}
\]
At every prior-net point, (37) gives
\[
 B_\delta^-(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,\delta}^+
 \leq\mathcal G(\lambda)\leq
 B_\delta^+(\lambda)-\sum_m\lambda_mc_{m,\delta}^-.             \tag{62}
\]
By the already established Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}quantitative\text{-}terminal\text{-}comparison}\), the width in (62) is at most
\[
 \bigl(B_\delta^+-B_\delta^-\bigr)
 \sum_m\lambda_m(c_{m,\delta}^+-c_{m,\delta}^-)
 \leq2\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\eta),                                 \tag{63}
\]
and \(\rho_{H,K}(\delta,\sqrt\delta)\to0\).  Equations (60)--(63), together with the validated point-mass recursions, give certified dual bounds including the oracle offsets.

For a finite policy mixture with weights \(p_s\), suppose the independent fixed-policy recursion gives scenario-risk intervals \([L_m^-,L_m^+]\) and the point-mass recursion gives oracle intervals \([c_m^-,c_m^+]\).  Then
\[
 V\leq\max_m\{L_m^+-c_m^-\}.                                    \tag{64}
\]
This upper endpoint is valid independently of the optimization recursion that selected the mixture.

All lower endpoints converge upward to \(V\) by (43), (52), (54), (58), and (60)--(63), as the prior radius, terminal width, guard-exit probability, state and control meshes, Gaussian cells and tails, and rounding errors vanish.  Every occurrence of scaled-datum continuity in this list is charged using \(\widetilde\Omega_\delta\).  For upper endpoints, take the finite \(\epsilon\)-saddle mixture of Markov Bayes responses supplied by Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}least\text{-}favorable\text{-}saddle}\).  A net prior within radius \(r_\lambda\) of its least-favorable prior makes each component \(2r_\lambda\)-Bayes, since both a fixed policy's Bayes risk and the Bayes value are \(1\)-Lipschitz in the prior.  Equations (56)--(57) approximate the finitely many components by enumerated grid policies, which are eventually retained.  Their mixture is feasible for the rational scenario-risk linear program, while (58), (63), and the independent recursion make (64) at most \(V+\epsilon+o(1)\).  Letting \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves downward convergence of the cumulative primal endpoints to \(V\).

Every candidate computation is finite.  Gaussian probabilities and elementary functions admit terminating rational Taylor enclosures on bounded cells, omitted tails use (58), and both optimization problems are finite rational linear programs.  The deterministic enumeration contains \(\delta\downarrow0\), \(\eta=\sqrt\delta\), \(G\uparrow\infty\), and the nested refinements in (52).  Recomputing every affected ledger term from (43) shows that the actual ledger sum tends to zero.  Thus, for every \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}>0\), some finite candidate has certified gap at most \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\), so the search reaches it and terminates.  Cumulative maxima of lower endpoints and minima of independently validated upper endpoints are monotone and valid.  At termination,
\[
 \underline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon},
 \qquad
 \overline V_{\varepsilon}-\underline V_{\varepsilon}
 \leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}},
\]
and the independently evaluated mixture satisfies
\(\max_mr_m(u)\leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}\).

Finally, \(\overline V_{\varepsilon}\leq V+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{cert}}\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}boundary\text{-}stable\text{-}frontier}\) transfers the returned mixture's scenario-risk vector to predictable finite-horizon policies and gives \(c_{n,m}\to c_m\).  Since \(M\) is finite,
\[
 \max_mr_{n,m}(\pi_n)=\max_mr_m(u)+o(1)
 \leq\overline V_{\varepsilon}+o(1).
\]
Only the exact finite scenario list and \(\lvert h_j^m\rvert\leq H\) were used; no null-boundary closure premise is needed.  The proof establishes termination and certified convergence, but no closed-form mesh size, arithmetic complexity bound, or convergence rate.
